These are this winter’s train times

Train companies change their timetables twice a year, and the summer one is not the same as the winter one. Some trains run at different times, and a few get added or taken away. A change that works well now may not work in summer.

Every time on this page comes from a winter weekend, so please treat it as a guide to how the trains run. When I last checked, the summer 2027 times had not been published. They usually come out in the spring, and I will update this page when they do. I have kept to the trains and changes that work well, so a journey planner may show a few more options.

          Pay less to get there

          Ways I have found to bring the cost of the trip down

          Book Advance tickets early

          An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out, so book as soon as the show dates are out.

          Train
          Think about an off peak ticket

          An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you do not know when you will want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

          Train
          Look at a railcard

          A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off too.

          Railcard

          Good to know

          Quick answers before you travel.

          Which station is closest to Shuttleworth?
          Biggleswade. It is about 3 miles from Old Warden, and it is the station the Shuttleworth shuttle bus runs from. Bedford is the other one people mention, but it is about 9.5 miles away, so I would stick with Biggleswade.
          How do I get from the station to the show?
          Shuttleworth runs its own shuttle bus from Biggleswade station on show days. In 2027 it is £10 return, and you book it when you buy your show tickets, with set times there and back. A taxi is the other way, about 10 minutes from the rank near the station, and I would book your taxi home before the day. Walking is 45 minutes to an hour along country roads, so I would not plan on it.
          Are the trains different on a Sunday?
          Yes. On a Saturday the trains run twice an hour each way, from London St Pancras. On a Sunday they are hourly, and the London trains run from Kings Cross instead. If you are starting at Gatwick, East Croydon, London Bridge, Blackfriars or Farringdon on a Sunday, you ride to St Pancras and walk across the road to Kings Cross, which takes about 5 minutes. The times on this page allow for that.
          Do I need a ticket for the show?
          Yes, and I would book it before you travel. That way you can add the shuttle bus at the same time and know your times there and back.
          What if my train is late or cancelled?
          Look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station. If you are on the shuttle bus, let the Shuttleworth team know, as the buses run at set times.
          I am coming from further away. What do I do?
          I would plan your trip to whichever station on this page is nearest to you, and pick it up from there. If you are coming from the south, Gatwick Airport and East Croydon are on the page, and on a Saturday their trains run straight through London to Biggleswade.

          Travelling with a disability or a buggy

          Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.

          • Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
          • Check the station has step free access to every platform you need, both ways.
